title: Ames/Davenant refuge-fiducia still only part of the last disposition — do not isolate one act
source_text: CXI. Plus ergo probabilitatis habet adhuc sententia Amesii, Davenantii, Petri Molinaei filii, & multorum aliorum superius allegatorum. Quae est praecipuum & specificum actum fidei justificantis, cui justificatio proprie tribuenda est, esse fiduciam illam qua Deo adhaeremus, eique innitimur, & ad misericordiam illius confugimus, ut gratiam & veniam ab eo impetremus. Sed ut ingenue dicam quid hac de re sentiam, non puto ita discerpendos & disjungendos esse fidei salvificae actus, ut uni, caeteris exclusis, tribuatur justificatio. Nam descripta fiducia est quidem pars illius ultimae, & proximae dispositionis cui promissum est Justificatio, & qua posita ponitur immediate & infallibiliter. Sed non sola illam constituit, & ad eandem dispositionem plures alii quoque actus pertinent.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore still more probability belongs to the opinion of Ames, Davenant, Pierre Du Moulin the son, and many others alleged above: that the chief and specific act of justifying faith, to which justification is properly to be attributed, is that trust by which we cling to God, lean on him, and flee to his mercy, so that we may obtain grace and pardon from him. But that I may say candidly what I think on this matter, I do not think the acts of saving faith should be so torn apart and disjoined that justification is attributed to one, the others excluded. For the fiducia described is indeed part of that last and nearest disposition to which justification is promised, and which being posited is posited immediately and infallibly. But it alone does not constitute that disposition, and several other acts also belong to the same disposition.
pass_b_english: Still more probable: Ames, Davenant, Pierre Du Moulin fils, and others — the chief specific act is refuge-fiducia: clinging to God, leaning on him, fleeing to his mercy for grace and pardon.
Le Blanc’s candid caveat: do not tear saving faith’s acts apart so justification is pinned on one alone.
Refuge-fiducia is part of the last proximate disposition that infallibly brings justification — but not the whole; other acts belong there too.
